quotation_allowlist.text: own product write-up says the product excludes
quotation_allowlist.why: VERIFIED VERBATIM, WITH A PROVENANCE RECORD IN THE REPO. insulation-garage-longmont.html quotes Xcel's exclusion list in a rebate bullet and in an FAQ answer. R1 half B is a STRING LIST, not a claim test -- it fires on a quote glyph near an attribution verb and has no way to see that a prose quotation is backed. The backing now exists: _shared_components.py CITED_SOURCES['XCEL_INSULATION_EXCLUSIONS'], quote=True with a complete {retrieved, artifact, extraction, verbatim_line} record. The PDF was fetched 2026-09-18 (sha256:1e683803bbddd998b1c988132583ddea3415d0bba55086bc7fe080cf20a2c271) and read with pdftotext -layout; lines 143-145 read 'This product excludes new residential construction, new residential additions, insulation of doors, garages, sheds, workshops, below-ground basements, mobile homes, projects with pre-improvement R-values of R-16 or greater, and residential properties with more than four units.' The page's quotation is exact and truncates with an ellipsis after 'mobile homes', dropping two further EXCLUSIONS -- a truncation that can only make the list more permissive, never more flattering to the reader's eligibility, and garages are named in both. SCOPED TO "own product write-up says the product excludes" RATHER THAN "its own ...": the identical verbatim quotation renders twice on this page with two different possessives, "its own" in the FAQ answer and "Xcel's own" in the rebate bullet, and the narrower string cleared only one of the two.

The claim is compliant; the page renders one quotation and the gate counted it twice. Scoped to the heading prefix so it cannot pardon any other sentence.

legitimate_uses: does publish a combined figure alongside
R4.legitimate_uses_reason: THE FIRST EIGHTEEN ARE COMMON.JSON'S LIST, COPIED VERBATIM AND NOT NARROWED, because _deep_merge REPLACES a list rather than unioning it -- dropping any of them here would silently un-declare a portfolio-wide legitimate use. Verified identical to common.json at canon 0b380c2 before copying. The six additions are LGM-only and each names an exact phrase, never a bare token. FIVE ARE BUILDING SCIENCE, not rebates: 'cures into a solid layer' (insulation-spray-foam: 'liquid polyurethane sprayed into a cavity, where it expands and cures into a solid layer'), 'thermal layer' (insulation-attic: 'the loose-fill or batted thermal layer installed across the floor of an unconditioned attic'), 'insulation layer' (llms.txt: 'cures into a solid air-sealing insulation layer'), 'flash layer' (hybrid-flash-batt: 'what puts the flash layer's thickness under the code'), and 'only layer between' (cathedral-ceiling: 'the roof deck itself is the only layer between conditioned space and outside'). None of the five can express two programs combining; each describes a physical course of material, which is the same class of legitimate use as 'stack effect' and 'plumbing stack' already in this list, and the brief's own protected example 'add radiant barrier on top of existing insulation'. THE SIXTH is a DIRECTOR-LICENSED ATTRIBUTED DESCRIPTION held as an unrendered record: _shared_components.py ALIVE_REBATES carries stacking_published_by_this_body, whose `what` field reads 'Efficiency Works' own insulation and air sealing incentive sheet prints an "Additional incentives" table with three columns ... so the administrator of this program does publish a combined figure alongside Xcel's.' ground-truth.md:27-44 licenses stacking to be DESCRIBED as published by Efficiency Works, WITH that attribution -- which this record carries in the adjacent attribution_required field -- and the record names no figure. It has ZERO render sites, verified: render_alive_rebates_html() emits only name+summary+status and its own docstring states it does not show this field, and the function itself has zero call sites. The gate reaches it only through the SRC surface, which exists for pre-render claims a page assembles at runtime; this string is never assembled into anything.

Efficiency Works' "Xcel rebate" column reconciles with no Xcel per-measure cap this repo has verified.' It is the instruction forbidding the site from stacking, recorded so the rule is not re-litigated -- exactly what this filter row is named for, 'retired prohibition preserved as a record'. Failing the property for carrying the sentence that forbids the defect is the rule returning the same verdict for a claim and its prohibition.

R5.magnitude_words_reason: COMMON.JSON'S SIXTEEN WORDS, COPIED VERBATIM (verified identical at canon 0b380c2) WITH EXACTLY ONE CHARACTER CHANGED: 'lose' is now ' lose', with a leading space. _deep_merge REPLACES a list, so the whole list has to be restated to change one entry. THE REASON, measured not asserted: magnitude_words are matched with word=False, i.e. as raw substrings, and 'lose' is a substring of 'cellu-lose' and of 'c-lose to'. That single collision produced 16 of this property's 59 R5 findings on 2026-09-18 -- every cellulose-settling sentence ('Loose-fill cellulose settles 10-20% over time') and every Louisville housing-age sentence ('close to half of Louisville housing units (46.0%) predate 1990', where the pattern also extracted the numeral '0%' out of '46.0%'). Neither is a magnitude claim about energy savings, which is what R5 exists to police; both fired on a word that is not in them. THIS IS A NARROWING OF AN OVER-MATCH, NOT AN EXEMPTION OF A CLAIM: has_any() is case-insensitive, so every genuine use still matches -- ' lose', ' loses', ' Lose', ' losing' all carry the leading space in running prose. Verified after the change: 'An under-filled or settled cellulose attic loses more heat in a Longmont winter' STILL MATCHES and is still adjudicated. The only construction this cannot see is a sentence whose very first character begins the word, which the gate's own sentence pool makes vanishingly rare and which is recorded here rather than left implicit. The underlying defect is in the matcher, not the word list; this is the narrowest fix available from config alone.
R5.recognised_publishers_reason: THE FIRST SEVENTEEN ARE COMMON.JSON'S LIST, COPIED VERBATIM (verified identical at canon 0b380c2); _deep_merge replaces a list, so it has to be restated to extend it. THREE ADDITIONS, all of them bodies this property already cites by name in its own CITED_SOURCES registry and none of them a loosening of what counts as attribution -- f_pub still requires an attribution VERB and still requires the publisher within 80 characters of the figure. 'Colorado Geospatial Portal' is the source of the LPC service-territory share (registry key LONGMONT_LPC_PARTIAL_ELECTRIC_TERRITORY, its statewide Utilities Boundaries layer) which this property discloses on fourteen pages and which the Director's brief records as CORRECT copy; it was absent from the list, so the sentences carrying that disclosure could not be cleared by naming their own source. 'U.S. Census Bureau' and 'Census Bureau' are the source of every town housing-age figure on this property (registry key CENSUS_ACS5_PLACE_HOUSING, ACS 5-year estimates 2020-2024); the area pages already name it inline in parentheses. A federal statistical agency and a state geospatial clearinghouse are publishers by any reading, and their absence was a gap in the list rather than a judgement about them.
